$comment: The loop's control surface. Read by loop-tick.yml (the reactor), by
scripts/loop-blast-radius.mjs (the contagion firewall), and by
scripts/gen-loop-data.mjs (which publishes it, minus nothing — there are
no secrets here and the whole point is that the governor is public).
`enabled` is the master switch and it is OFF. Every loop workflow checks it
first and exits 0. Turning it on is a deliberate, reviewable commit — the
same shape as ANNOUNCE in bsky-hello.yml and BOT_ENABLED in the factory,
and for the same reason: the expensive, irreversible half of this system
should start with a diff someone signed.
writes targets plant/**, NOT foam/**. foam/ is HAND-AUTHORED and the loop never
writes there — that is the contamination boundary (docs/LOOP-SPRINTS.md §1).
plant/ is the loop's own tree, seeded from foam. It has no deploy workflow yet,
so nothing it writes reaches the internet until a surface is registered.
COLD START: the reactor wakes on a push touching THIS FILE or runs.jsonl.
workflow_dispatch cannot be used — loop-tick.yml does not exist on the default
branch, and GitHub 404s a dispatch at a workflow it cannot see there. Editing
this file is the designed way to start a run from cold.
First live dispatch (2026-08-04) passed all four gates and then failed to push:
actions/checkout persists its token as an http extraheader that overrides the
remote URL's credentials, so the PAT was ignored. Fixed with
persist-credentials: false. See the dead-end bead.
TURN 2 (2026-08-05). Turn 1 completed and produced nothing: the commit step
staged .github/loop/ and loop/ but not plant/, so the agent's files died with
the runner. Staging is now derived from `writes`. And beads carry a `gate`
array that loop-work RUNS after the turn — turn 1 correctly reported it could
not verify its own acceptance test, having no Bash.
COLD START for the PLAN SEAT (2026-08-05). The previous starvation halt wrote
its plan request and then died before committing it: the Decide step re-ran
loop-tick to read the halt reason, and that rerun also exits 3 under errexit.
COLD START #2 for the PLAN SEAT. That fix worked — the halt path set
acted=plan — and the tick STILL failed, one step later: `git add` on
.github/loop/work/ is fatal when there are no work orders, and a starved tick
by definition has none. The request was written on the runner and deleted with
the workspace. Staging now skips paths that do not exist, --json stdout is
machine-clean, and the CLI's process contract has a regression test.
THE TAP IS OPEN. Three planner-authored beads promoted by the operator —
lp-6b641c, lp-687d8d, lp-138b76 — the loop's first queue it wrote itself.
This cold start dispatches turn 3, and from here the chain self-continues:
work -> verdict -> runs.jsonl -> tick -> work. It stops on its own when the
dispatchable queue drains, because the planner's output is born `proposed`
and only a human promotes. That resting state is the design, not a stall.
Bounds in force this run: turnsPerRun 1, turnsPerDay 12 (2 spent),
hardStopTurns 40, maxConcurrentWork 2, repeatedGateFailures 2. See the
finding on class-A self-certification recorded at promotion time.
The budget is the controller, not a limit (CLOSED-LOOP.md §8). The
reactor reads these and decides where the marginal turn pays; it does not
merely count down. `hardStopTurns` is the backstop that exists because a
controller with a bug is still a loop.
These numbers are guesses. Phase 1's second job is to replace them with a
measurement — the estimate in CLOSED-LOOP.md §10 is flagged there as the
weakest number in the document, and it still is.
ALL THREE ARE STOP CONDITIONS, and a loop that cannot stop is the failure
mode rather than the feature (CLOSED-LOOP.md §6.2). `noImprovementTurns`
is the interesting one: it is the measurement this whole programme exists
to take, wired up as a brake.
Three signals, deliberately not one model call. Disagreement between them
is itself data (CLOSED-LOOP.md §6.2). `weights` are placeholders until the
pilot's human scores calibrate them — an uncalibrated judge is a number,
not a measurement, and publishing it as one would be the exact mistake
this repo keeps writing down.
THE ORG CHART, and it is PROPOSED — not yet wired to anything. Published
because the governor being public is the point (LOOP-WBS.md §3.4).
A seat is a licence to occupy one concurrent turn. `total` is the supply
constraint and it is EXOGENOUS: nothing inside the loop can raise it. The
allocator only distributes what the operator has already granted.
`review` is capped at 1 deliberately. Promotion costs a review seat, so the
rate at which the loop can feed its own queue is priced rather than
prohibited — that cap IS the gain control.
STATUS 'partial': the PLAN seat is wired and live (loop-plan.yml). The
allocator does not exist yet — plan is staffed by one specific signal, a
starved queue, which is the allocator's first real behaviour rather than the
allocator itself. implement is the existing loop-work. review, judge and merge
remain proposed.

plan.does: Decomposes a spec into requirements that meet the Definition of Ready.
plan.staffedWhen: the reactor finds NO DISPATCHABLE work — live, via .github/loop/plan/request.json

implement.does: One class-A requirement, start to finish. No Bash, no git, no network.

review.does: Validates a proposal and promotes it. Never one it authored.
review.staffedWhen: proposals pile up unpromoted — capped at 1: this is the gain control

judge.does: Scores a completed sprint against the gates and the ladder.

merge.does: The integrator. Merges the sprint, applies every outbox, regenerates, deploys.
merge.staffedWhen: at the barrier only — serialized by construction
